title: The 5 People Who Spent the Most Time in Space, Ranked (#1 Passed 3 Years)

scenes.text: The five people who've spent the most days off the planet. Number one passed a thousand.

scenes.label: Aleksandr Kaleri · 769 days
scenes.text: Number five: Aleksandr Kaleri. 769 days over five flights, from the Mir station in 1992 to the space station in 2011.

scenes.label: Sergei Krikalev · 803 days
scenes.text: Number four: Sergei Krikalev, 803 days. He held the record for almost ten years.

scenes.label: Yuri Malenchenko · 827 days
scenes.text: Number three: Yuri Malenchenko, 827 days. In 2003 he got married from orbit, with his bride in Texas.

scenes.label: Gennady Padalka · 878 days
scenes.text: Number two: Gennady Padalka. 878 days across five missions.

scenes.label: Oleg Kononenko · 1,111 days
scenes.text: Number one: Oleg Kononenko. In June 2024 he became the first human to reach a thousand days in space. He landed with 1,111. Over three years of his life, off Earth.

description:
The five people who have spent the most total time in space, ranked by cumulative days across all their flights.
Oleg Kononenko leads with 1,111 days over five missions, after passing 1,000 days in June 2024 and landing that September. Then come Gennady Padalka (878 days), Yuri Malenchenko (827), Sergei Krikalev (803) and Aleksandr Kaleri (769). All five are Russian cosmonauts who flew long stays on Mir, the International Space Station or both.
Could you spend three years of your life in orbit?
first_comment: Kononenko's 1,111 days are spread over five missions; the longest single flight is still Valeri Polyakov's 437 days. Who would you put at number one, and what should we rank next?
